svg.title: Signing away death row: Newsom commutes California's death sentences
svg.desc: Editorial illustration. Seen from behind, over his shoulder, Gov. Gavin Newsom, with slicked-back dark hair greying at the temples and a navy suit, signs a letter under a green desk lamp in a dark office at dusk. A tall tower of case folders rises beside him, a California bear flag hangs nearby, and through a tall window a distant generic prison's long cell blocks glow with rows of small lit windows under a rose and amber sky. Represents Newsom commuting all 548 California death sentences to life without parole on Nov. 5, 2026; the folder tower is a symbol, and the office and prison are not specific places.
